articleSummary: Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), detected in 2017, has spread to more than two dozen states, including New York, Massachusetts, South Carolina, Oklahoma, and Missouri. articleHeadline: Tiny RNA Molecule Pushes Schistosome Parasites Toward Self-Destruction
articleSummary: Schistosoma japonicum, a major cause of human and animal schistosomiasis in Asia, may be steered toward apoptosis by a single microRNA, sja-miR-2a-3p. In permissive BALB/c mice, parasites flourish; in less-permissive Wistar rats they exhibit higher apoptotic activity. Expression of sja-miR-2a-3p is elevated during 14–28 days post-infection, especially in schistosomula from Wistar rats, with tissue enrichment in the male testis and posterior region and in the female vitellaria. Computational targets include several apoptosis-related genes; functional tests in vitro showed that mimics or inhibitors of sja-miR-2a-3p modulate apoptosis gene transcripts and egg output, with TUNEL staining confirming DNA fragmentation. Findings link host environment, parasite apoptosis, and a regulatory RNA, hinting at new control strategies that disrupt parasite survival by targeting its own gene regulation. articleSummary: Five-year national TB screening in the Netherlands (2019–2023) analyzed 149,214 migrants to map active TB and latent infection in a low-incidence setting. Immigrants (87,511) yielded 69 TB cases (79/100k); asylum seekers (61,703) yielded 170 cases (276/100k). Country-level yields exceeded birth-country WHO incidence for asylum seekers, with Sierra Leone (888), Eritrea (704), Somalia (581), Gambia (562) and South Sudan/Sudan (519) top; immigrants’ highest yields were Indonesia (291) and the Philippines (241). Symptom-based detection was weak: of 202 screen-detected pulmonary TB cases, 27.2% reported cough (immigrants 13.8%, asylum seekers 32.6%). About 56.5% of 239 screen-detected TB cases were bacteriologically confirmed; two MDR-TB cases. Treatment outcomes: immigrants 92.8% cured/completed vs asylum seekers 81.2%, with loss to follow-up and cross-border movement driving the gap. A second component analyzed latent infection in >20,000 immigrants, rising with age (0.6% under 12, 4.4% among adolescent). Implications for Europe include radiological screening value and cross-border care continuity.

articleSummary: Drug-resistant TB risk is rising among cutaneous tuberculosis patients, per a Lucknow-based study from King George’s Medical University (KGMU). In 54 cutaneous TB cases (ages 20–40) studied between 2019–2022, seven developed drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) and were HIV-negative. Six did not respond to the most effective anti-TB drug and received multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) regimens; one patient showed resistance to another primary TB drug. Diagnosis is challenging due to low bacillary loads; CBNAAT and culture are recommended, and whole-genome sequencing may improve future detection. Treatment duration ranges from 9 to 18 months, and early identification of DR-TB is crucial to prevent spread to the chest or CNS.

articleSummary: West Nile virus infections are reported in Italy and Brazil in 2026. Italy has 41 deaths and 594 confirmed cases through September 8, per the ISS weekly bulletin. In Brazil, four confirmed cases in 2026 with one death, affecting São Paulo and Santa Catarina. West Nile virus is a flavivirus first identified in Uganda in 1937 and now circulating across multiple regions. It is transmitted mainly by Culex mosquitoes; birds, especially migratory species, are natural reservoirs. Most infections are asymptomatic; about 20% develop mild illness with abrupt fever, malaise, anorexia, nausea, headache, myalgias, rash, and lymphadenopathy. A small proportion progress to neuroinvasive disease (meningitis, encephalitis, paralysis). No antiviral or human vaccine exists; management is supportive, with hospitalization or ICU as needed. Prevention includes repellents, screens, eliminating standing water, sanitation, and avoiding handling dead animals.

articleHeadline: Hepatitis A Immunity Stays High in Urban India While Hepatitis E Exposure
articleSummary: In urban Vellore, southern India, IgG serology for hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV) was measured in two cross-sectional cohorts (2013: n=600; 2022: n=558), ages 1–40. HAV immunity remained highly endemic and uniform across years: seroprevalence >80% among 1–5-year-olds and 100% by age 16+, with no statistically significant year-to-year differences. HEV exposure stayed low in youth and increased gradually with age; among adults 26–40, seroprevalence rose from 18% (2013) to 24% (2022), a non-significant change. Cluster analyses showed HAV seroprevalence was uniformly high across neighborhoods, while HEV exposure was low and heterogeneous, indicating localized risk factors. The estimated effective reproduction number for HAV (Re) was below 1 in both surveys, implying no sustained secondary transmission. Findings reflect a stable HAV-endemic milieu amid urban development and a patchy, slowly accumulating HEV exposure, with surveillance implications.

The northeastern Ituri province is the main center, with transmission spreading to the east and north and new cases in South Ubangi near CAR and Congo-Brazzaville. Government spokesman Patrick Muyaya said the peak was passed in the first half of August and indicators show a decline; 10 of 61 health zones have had no new cases for at least 21 days. articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) persists as of 13 September 2026, with 7,022 cases and 3,398 deaths across 62 health zones in seven provinces. On 10 September, South Ubangi province reported its first case in the Bulu health zone; the index case was a 23-year-old man from South Kivu who left July 10. The World Health Organization end criterion requires no confirmed or probable cases for 42 days (twice the 21-day incubation), counted from the last possible transmission. The start of the countdown depends on case outcomes: if the patient survives, it begins the day after the second negative test; if they die in a treatment center, it begins after secure burial; if buried in the community, it begins after burial. Fifteen zones crossed 21 days without a case and then relapsed since July; by 6 September, nine zones exceeded 21 days. The 2018–2020 North Kivu outbreak serves as precedent, but end declarations do not close the dossier due to possible resurgences (Butembo 2021, Beni 2022).

articleSummary: As of 13 September 2026, in Indonesia, pediatric influenza cases have risen, spreading rapidly in public spaces and schools. The article distinguishes influenza A and B. Influenza A transmits widely and can involve animals, carrying pandemic potential (historically linked to the 2009 H1N1 outbreak). Influenza B spreads by human-to-human transmission, remains seasonal but can cause severe pneumonia in children and other vulnerable groups; global seasonal deaths are estimated at 290,000–650,000 annually. Flu is not the same as the common cold: influenza A and B cause abrupt onset fever, cough, muscle aches, headaches, fatigue, and sometimes vomiting or diarrhea in children. Laboratory testing is the definitive method to confirm whether a child has influenza A, influenza B, or a cold. Vaccination is recommended to protect children; parents should monitor for sudden, severe symptoms and seek care promptly.

Most cases remain concentrated in Ituri, including infections detected in schools after the summer break, heightening parental and healthcare worker concerns. articleSummary: Uganda imposes a 21-day supervised quarantine on students arriving from the Democratic Republic of Congo before entering or rejoining Ugandan schools. articleSummary: Six-minute detection of antibodies against H5N1 avian influenza achieved by a multichannel electronic tongue developed at the University of São Carlos (USP) Institute of Physics (IFSC). The platform uses renewable-protein coatings—zein from corn, jacalin from jackfruit, and concanavalin A from beans—to modify gold nanoparticles, forming four sensors that generate an electrical fingerprint when antibodies bind to H5N1. Coupled with machine learning, it differentiates H5N1-positive samples from healthy and other avian diseases with 98.6% accuracy. The device targets clinical and veterinary contexts, enabling rapid surveillance to map regions and species exposure and aid early containment of outbreaks. Although promising, calibration sensitivity and sensor wear pose challenges for commercialization. The approach offers a low-cost, rapid alternative for detecting avian influenza antibodies and could be adapted to other viral targets.

articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached a turning point, described as the worst outbreak on record. As of September 1, there are more than 6,186 lab-confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths since May, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC. The outbreak began in the mining area of Mongbalu in Ituri Province in late April, spreading through connected communities and health networks to Rwampara and Bunia, and crossing into Uganda.
